text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Former deputy of the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) Frantisek Gaulieder said he would appeal to the Constitutional Court against the withdrawal of his mandate in parliament on Wednesday.
- The government is considering preparing a law to protect domestic producers against "excessive imports".

- The government will issue bonds worth some eight billion crowns next year to provide starting funds for the planned ExIm bank. The cabinet has also approved a two billion crown contribution for the ExIm bank from the 1997 state budget, which will be the bank's basic capital.

- Tyre producer Matador Puchov will issue a 500 million crown tranche of three-year bonds on December 13. The bond will carry a coupon equivalent to the central bank's discount rate plus 3.35 percentage points.
- Matador will issue bonds worth 700 million crowns next year in unspecified tranches.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Troubled heavy engineering company and arms maker ZTS Dubnica, and Germany's Sauer-Sundstrand GmbH have created a joint-venture to produce pumps and engines.
- Overall debts of ZTS Dubnica now total five billion crowns.
- Agriculture ministers of the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) begin a one-day summit in Bratislava on Thursday.
- Slovak beer producers said they expect the government to approve a beer import limit of 200,000 hectolitres a year for 1997.
- Pharmaceuticals producer Biotika said it planned turnover of more than one billion crowns next year.
PRAVDA - The opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) said it would not support the 1997 draft budget mainly due to shortcomings in the social sector.
